walkthrough: A hadron is made of quarks; a lepton is a fundamental particle and is not made of quarks.

hints: Balance charge and nucleon number, and identify the neutral lepton accompanying beta-plus decay.
walkthrough: A proton changes into a neutron, so the emitted charged particle is a positron. An electron neutrino is also emitted.
$^{1}_{1}\mathrm p\rightarrow{}^{1}_{0}\mathrm n+{}^{0}_{+1}\mathrm e+{}^{0}_{0}\nu_e$. The nucleon numbers total 1 and the charges total +1 on both sides.

hints: Beta decay changes one quark flavour into another.
walkthrough: The decay is caused by the weak nuclear interaction.

hints: Choose three distinct conserved quantities; mass alone is not conserved separately from energy.
walkthrough: Three suitable quantities are total mass-energy, momentum and electric charge.
Nucleon number is also conserved in this decay. State any three accepted distinct quantities.

hints: Write the proton’s three quarks, then add their charges.
walkthrough: A proton contains two up quarks and one down quark: uud.
Each up quark has charge $+2e/3$ and the down quark has charge $-e/3$.
